lines.trans: Clara, Rocio told us there is a secret ninth room.
My little brother grabbed the tape measure before finishing his toast.
Come in, both of you! Tell me if the room is safe.
Four metres wide, six long, a brick wall and a wooden ceiling.
Listen: you clap once and you can hardly hear the street.

words.gloss: you give (das una palmada = you clap)
one; you (se oye = can be heard)

lines.trans: Zero echo! Wood and glass are perfect for soft music.
So Rocio's cafe and Carmen's piano are not going to wake the guests?
Not at all. The thick brick wall cuts the noise from the stairs.
This weekend I am not working at City Hall, Clara. Put us to work!
Can you help bring up the tables from the cellar after lunch?
With pleasure! Working with Javier is better than sitting in an office.
First I will sketch the window latches. Fresh air has to come in from the courtyard.

meanings.note: Marks destination, clock time, and animate direct objects (personal a).

examples.text: Vamos a la estación ahora.
examples.trans: We are going to the station now.

examples.text: El desayuno empieza a las ocho.
examples.trans: Breakfast starts at eight o'clock.

meanings.note: Al aire libre means 'outdoors'.

examples.text: El aire es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The air is very important here.

examples.text: Hablamos sobre el aire.
examples.trans: We talk about the air.

meanings.note: Opposite of estrecho (narrow).

examples.text: Es una pieza ancha.
examples.trans: It is a wide piece.

examples.text: ¡Cuidado, Ernesto, la jarra tiene la boca muy ancha!
examples.trans: Careful, Ernesto, the pitcher has a very wide spout!

meanings.note: Antes de means 'before' a noun or infinitive.

examples.text: Llegué diez minutos antes.
examples.trans: I arrived ten minutes early.

examples.text: Antes de salir, cierra la ventana.
examples.trans: Before leaving, close the window.

meanings.note: Regular -ar verb; ayudar a + infinitive.

examples.text: ¿Te ayudo con esas dos cajas?
examples.trans: Shall I help you with those two boxes?

examples.text: Siempre ayudamos a los nuevos vecinos.
examples.trans: We always help the new neighbours.

meanings.note: Municipal government building and town council in Spain.

examples.text: El ayuntamiento está aquí.
examples.trans: The City Hall is here.

examples.text: Vemos los ayuntamientos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the City Halls from the door.

meanings.note: Plural los cafés (two coffees = dos cafés).

examples.text: El café está aquí.
examples.trans: The coffee is here.

examples.text: Vemos los cafés desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the coffees from the door.

meanings.note: Feminine noun: la calle.

examples.text: La calle está aquí.
examples.trans: The street is here.

examples.text: Vemos las calles desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the streets from the door.

meanings.note: Placed before the word it modifies.

examples.text: Ya son casi las doce.
examples.trans: It is almost twelve o'clock already.

examples.text: Casi olvido la llave en la mesa.
examples.trans: I nearly forgot the key on the table.

meanings.note: Used for numbers, temperatures, and emphatic 'zero!'.

examples.text: Hoy tenemos cero problemas.
examples.trans: Today we have zero problems.

examples.text: El marcador está a cero.
examples.trans: The score is at zero.

meanings.note: Metal clasp or fastener on a chest or bag.

examples.text: El cierre está aquí.
examples.trans: The latch is here.

examples.text: Vemos los cierres desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the latchs from the door.

meanings.note: Silk ribbon or adhesive tape.

examples.text: La cinta está aquí.
examples.trans: The ribbon is here.

examples.text: Vemos las cintas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the ribbons from the door.

coger.gloss: to take; to pick up; to catch (Spain)

meanings.en: to take; to pick up; to catch (Spain)
meanings.note: Standard everyday Peninsula Spanish verb for picking up objects or taking transport (g -> j before o: cojo).

examples.text: Cojo el autobús cada mañana.
examples.trans: I take the bus every morning.

examples.text: Coge una taza limpia del estante.
examples.trans: Take a clean cup from the shelf.

meanings.note: Regular -er verb.

examples.text: Comemos juntos a las dos de la tarde.
examples.trans: We have lunch together at two in the afternoon.

examples.text: Comí un trozo de bizcocho de limón.
examples.trans: I ate a piece of lemon sponge cake.

meanings.note: Combines with mí/ti to form conmigo ('with me') and contigo ('with you').

examples.text: Tomo café con leche caliente.
examples.trans: I take coffee with hot milk.

examples.text: Habla con calma, por favor.
examples.trans: Speak calmly, please.

meanings.note: Regular -ar verb.

examples.text: Corto el pan en rebanadas finas.
examples.trans: I slice the bread into thin slices.

examples.text: La panadera cortó cuatro trozos de bizcocho.
examples.trans: The baker cut four pieces of sponge cake.

meanings.note: Refers to window glass or crystal.

examples.text: El cristal está aquí.
examples.trans: The windowpane is here.

examples.text: Vemos los cristales desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the windowpanes from the door.

meanings.note: Invariable cardinal number.

examples.text: Tenemos cuatro mesas dentro.
examples.trans: We have four tables inside.

examples.text: La habitación cuatro da al patio.
examples.trans: Room four looks out onto the courtyard.

dar.gloss: to give; to face onto (dar a); to strike (the hour)

meanings.en: to give; to face onto (dar a); to strike (the hour)
meanings.note: Irregular 1st sg doy and preterite di/dio; dar las doce = strike twelve.

examples.text: La ventana da al patio soleado.
examples.trans: The window looks out onto the sunny courtyard.

examples.text: El reloj acaba de dar las doce.
examples.trans: The clock has just struck twelve.

meanings.note: Links possession, origin, material (de madera), and contents (taza de té).

examples.text: Es una mesa redonda de madera.
examples.trans: It is a round wooden table.

examples.text: Vengo de la estación de tren.
examples.trans: I am coming from the train station.

meanings.note: Querer decir means 'to mean'.

examples.text: ¿Qué dice la carta exactamente?
examples.trans: What does the letter say exactly?

examples.text: Dime la verdad sin miedo.
examples.trans: Tell me the truth without fear.

meanings.note: Mandatory contraction of preposition de + masculine article el.

examples.text: El bizcocho acaba de salir del horno.
examples.trans: The cake just came out of the oven.

examples.text: Soy vecino del barrio.
examples.trans: I am a neighbour from the quarter.

meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (e -> ie: despierta).

examples.text: Me despierto temprano sin reloj.
examples.trans: I wake up early without an alarm.

examples.text: El olor a café despertó a toda la casa.
examples.trans: The smell of coffee woke the whole house.

meanings.note: Después de + noun/infinitive means 'after'.

examples.text: Hablamos después del desayuno.
examples.trans: We will talk after breakfast.

examples.text: ¿Qué hacemos después de eso?
examples.trans: What do we do after that?

meanings.note: Regular -ar verb; the noun is el dibujo, a drawing.

examples.text: Mi hija dibuja un gato.
examples.trans: My daughter is drawing a cat.

examples.text: ¿Me dibujas el camino al hotel?
examples.trans: Will you sketch me the way to the hotel?

meanings.note: Los dos / las dos means 'both'.

examples.text: Pongo dos tazas azules en la mesa.
examples.trans: I put two blue cups on the table.

examples.text: Compra las dos válvulas por favor.
examples.trans: Buy both valves, please.

meanings.note: Reflected sound in a courtyard or hall.

examples.text: El eco está aquí.
examples.trans: The echo is here.

examples.text: Vemos los ecos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the echos from the door.

meanings.note: Definite article; also appears before feminine nouns starting with stressed /a/ (el agua, el asa).

examples.text: El patio tiene mucha luz.
examples.trans: The courtyard has plenty of light.

examples.text: Pásame el libro de reservas.
examples.trans: Pass me the reservation book.

meanings.note: Expresses location inside or on top of a surface (en la mesa = on the table).

examples.text: Las tazas están en la mesa.
examples.trans: The cups are on the table.

examples.text: Vivimos en Valencia todo el año.
examples.trans: We live in Valencia all year.

meanings.note: Desde entonces = since then.

examples.text: ¿Entonces nos vemos mañana a las ocho?
examples.trans: So shall we see each other tomorrow at eight?

examples.text: Desde entonces trabaja con nosotros.
examples.trans: Since then she works with us.

entrar.gloss: to come in; to go in; to enter

meanings.en: to come in; to go in; to enter
meanings.note: Pairs with en in Spain (entrar en la posada).

examples.text: Entra mucha luz por el balcón.
examples.trans: Plenty of light comes in through the balcony.

examples.text: Entramos en la tienda para resguardarnos.
examples.trans: We stepped into the shop to shelter.

meanings.note: Often singular (la escalera) or plural (las escaleras) for a staircase.

examples.text: La escalera está aquí.
examples.trans: The stairs is here.

examples.text: Vemos las escaleras desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the stairss from the door.

meanings.note: Needs no preposition for 'to' before things (escucha el agua).

examples.text: Escucho los pájaros desde mi cama.
examples.trans: I listen to the birds from my bed.

examples.text: Escuchamos la lluvia sobre las tejas.
examples.trans: We listened to the rain on the tiles.

meanings.note: Pairs with locations (está en el patio) and temporary states (está caliente).

examples.text: El desayuno ya está listo.
examples.trans: Breakfast is ready now.

examples.text: ¿Dónde están las llaves de latón?
examples.trans: Where are the brass keys?

meanings.note: Forms: este (m sg), esta (f sg), estos (m pl), estas (f pl).

examples.text: Este patio es muy tranquilo.
examples.trans: This courtyard is very quiet.

examples.text: Esta mañana hace mucho sol.
examples.trans: This morning it is very sunny.

meanings.note: Por fin = finally.

examples.text: El fin está aquí.
examples.trans: The end is here.

examples.text: Vemos los fines desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the ends from the door.

meanings.note: Pintura fresca = wet paint; agua fresca = cool water.

examples.text: Es una pieza fresca.
examples.trans: It is a cool piece.

examples.text: Bien. Pon estas hierbas frescas por encima antes de servirlos.
examples.trans: Good. Put these fresh herbs on top before serving them.

meanings.note: Describes thick envelopes, walls, or coats.

examples.text: Es una pieza gruesa.
examples.trans: It is a thick piece.

examples.text: este sobre grueso
examples.trans: this thick envelope

meanings.note: ¡Mucho gusto! = Pleased to meet you!; estar a gusto = to feel comfortable.

examples.text: El gusto es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The pleasure is very important here.

examples.text: Hablamos sobre el gusto.
examples.trans: We talk about the pleasure.

meanings.note: Impersonal present form hay means 'there is / there are'; haber que + infinitive = must / need to.

examples.text: Hay pan caliente en la cocina.
examples.trans: There is warm bread in the kitchen.

examples.text: Ya hemos preparado las habitaciones.
examples.trans: We have already prepared the rooms.

meanings.note: Plural habitaciones.

examples.text: La habitación está aquí.
examples.trans: The room is here.

examples.text: Vemos las habitaciones desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the rooms from the door.

meanings.note: Hermano mayor = older brother; hermano pequeño = younger brother.

examples.text: El hermano está aquí.
examples.trans: The brother is here.

examples.text: Vemos los hermanos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the brothers from the door.

meanings.note: Plural los huéspedes.

examples.text: El huésped está aquí.
examples.trans: The overnight guest is here.

examples.text: Vemos los huéspedes desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the overnight guests from the door.

meanings.note: Ir a + infinitive expresses near future ('going to do').

examples.text: Voy a abrir la puerta ahora.
examples.trans: I am going to open the door now.

examples.text: ¿Cómo va todo esta mañana?
examples.trans: How is everything going this morning?

meanings.note: Definite feminine singular article before nouns; direct-object feminine pronoun before/attached to verbs.

examples.text: La puerta del patio es azul.
examples.trans: The courtyard door is blue.

examples.text: La habitación tiene mucha luz.
examples.trans: The room has plenty of light.

meanings.note: De ladrillo = made of brick.

examples.text: El ladrillo está aquí.
examples.trans: The brick is here.

examples.text: Vemos los ladrillos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the bricks from the door.

meanings.note: Superlative larguísimo = very long.

examples.text: ¡Qué día tan largo en la posada!
examples.trans: What a long day at the inn!

examples.text: El pasillo es largo y oscuro.
examples.trans: The hallway is long and dark.

meanings.note: Used with feminine plural nouns and clock hours (las ocho).

examples.text: Las ventanas dan al jardín.
examples.trans: The windows face the garden.

examples.text: Desayunamos a las ocho.
examples.trans: We have breakfast at eight.

meanings.note: Los viernes means 'every Friday / on Fridays'.

examples.text: Los vecinos vienen a desayunar.
examples.trans: The neighbours come for breakfast.

examples.text: Daba clases de piano los viernes.
examples.trans: She taught piano lessons on Fridays.

meanings.note: De madera = wooden.

examples.text: La madera está aquí.
examples.trans: The wood is here.

examples.text: Vemos las maderas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the woods from the door.

meanings.note: Irregular comparative/superlative of bueno; plural mejores.

examples.text: Esta ventana tiene la mejor vista.
examples.trans: This window has the best view.

examples.text: Hoy el radiador calienta mejor.
examples.trans: Today the radiator heats better.

meanings.note: Dining, cafe, or courtyard table.

examples.text: La mesa está aquí.
examples.trans: The table is here.

examples.text: Vemos las mesas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the tables from the door.

meanings.note: Unit of length (diez metros) or city metro.

examples.text: El metro está aquí.
examples.trans: The metre is here.

examples.text: Vemos los metros desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the metres from the door.

meanings.note: Plural mis (mi llave / mis llaves); unaccented, distinct from pronoun mí.

examples.text: Mi maleta es azul marino.
examples.trans: My suitcase is navy blue.

examples.text: Mis apuntes están en el bolsillo.
examples.trans: My notes are in my pocket.

meanings.note: Agrees before nouns (mucha agua, muchos años); invariable after verbs (llueve mucho).

examples.text: Hoy tenemos mucho trabajo.
examples.trans: Today we have a lot of work.

examples.text: Muchas gracias por el café.
examples.trans: Thank you very much for the coffee.

meanings.note: Mostly heard in la cinta métrica, the tape measure.

examples.text: ¿Tienes una cinta métrica?
examples.trans: Do you have a tape measure?

examples.text: Usamos el sistema métrico.
examples.trans: We use the metric system.

meanings.note: Clases de música = music lessons.

examples.text: La música es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The music is very important here.

examples.text: Hablamos sobre la música.
examples.trans: We talk about the music.

nada.gloss: nothing; not at all (de nada = you're welcome)

meanings.en: nothing; not at all (de nada = you're welcome)
meanings.note: No pasa nada = no problem; nada de... = no ... at all.

examples.text: Tranquilo, no pasa nada.
examples.trans: Easy now, there is no problem at all.

examples.text: No queda nada de mantequilla.
examples.trans: There is no butter left at all.

meanings.note: Placed directly before the verb (or object pronouns) to negate a sentence.

examples.text: Hoy no llueve en Valencia.
examples.trans: Today it is not raining in Valencia.

examples.text: No se preocupe por la hora.
examples.trans: Do not worry about the time.

nos.gloss: us; to us; each other (¡Nos vemos!)

meanings.en: us; to us; each other (¡Nos vemos!)
meanings.note: First-person plural object/reflexive/reciprocal pronoun.

examples.text: ¡Nos vemos mañana por la mañana!
examples.trans: See you tomorrow morning!

examples.text: Nos alegra mucho la noticia.
examples.trans: The news makes us very glad.

meanings.note: Agrees with its noun: la novena llave.

examples.text: Es una pieza novena.
examples.trans: It is a ninth piece.

examples.text: ¡¿Una novena llave de latón?! ¡¿La abrimos esta noche o esperamos a mañana?!
examples.trans: A ninth brass key?! Do we open it tonight or wait until morning?!

meanings.note: Workplace or municipal desk.

examples.text: La oficina está aquí.
examples.trans: The office is here.

examples.text: Vemos las oficinas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the offices from the door.

meanings.note: Irregular: oigo, oyes, oye, oímos, oís, oyen; ¡Oiga! / ¡Oye! gets someone's attention.

examples.text: ¿Me oyes bien por teléfono?
examples.trans: Can you hear me clearly on the phone?

examples.text: Acabo de oír pasos en la escalera.
examples.trans: I just heard footsteps on the stairs.

meanings.note: From palma, the palm of the hand: dar una palmada = to clap once.

examples.text: El profesor da una palmada y todos callan.
examples.trans: The teacher claps once and everyone goes quiet.

examples.text: Le da una palmada en la espalda.
examples.trans: He gives him a pat on the back.

meanings.note: Marks destination, recipient (para ti), deadline, and minutes to the hour (cinco para las doce).

examples.text: Este paquete blanco es para mi hermano.
examples.trans: This white parcel is for my brother.

examples.text: Faltan diez minutos para las doce.
examples.trans: It is ten minutes to twelve.

meanings.note: Feminine noun: la pared, las paredes.

examples.text: La pared está aquí.
examples.trans: The wall is here.

examples.text: Vemos las paredes desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the walls from the door.

pasar.gloss: to pass; to come in (¡Pase!); to happen

meanings.en: to pass; to come in (¡Pase!); to happen
meanings.note: ¿Qué pasa? = What's wrong?; No pasa nada = No problem.

examples.text: ¡Pase, por favor, y siéntese!
examples.trans: Come in, please, and have a seat!

examples.text: Pasa la farmacia verde a la derecha.
examples.trans: Pass the green pharmacy on your right.

meanings.note: Traditional inner courtyard at the heart of a Spanish building.

examples.text: El patio está aquí.
examples.trans: The courtyard is here.

examples.text: Vemos los patios desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the courtyards from the door.

meanings.note: Hermano pequeño = younger brother; de pequeño = as a child.

examples.text: Es una pieza pequeña.
examples.trans: It is a small piece.

examples.text: Hay una pequeña tarjeta de cartón atada al asa.
examples.trans: There is a small cardboard card tied to the handle.

meanings.note: Used alone as 'Perfect!'.

examples.text: Es una pieza perfecta.
examples.trans: It is a perfect piece.

examples.text: La clienta de la habitación cuatro se queda toda la semana. ¡Todo debe estar perfecto!
examples.trans: The guest in room four is staying all week. Everything must be perfect!

meanings.note: Tocar el piano = to play the piano.

examples.text: Por las tardes alguien toca una melodía suave en el viejo piano del salón.
examples.trans: In the afternoons someone plays a gentle melody on the old parlor piano.

examples.text: Hace veinticinco años daba clases de piano muy cerca de esta calle.
examples.trans: Twenty-five years ago I gave piano lessons very close to this street.

poder.gloss: can; to be able to; may

meanings.en: can; to be able to; may
meanings.note: Irregular: puedo, pude, podría.

examples.text: ¿Puedo ver la etiqueta otra vez?
examples.trans: May I look at the tag again?

examples.text: Hoy podemos desayunar en el patio.
examples.trans: Today we can have breakfast in the courtyard.

poner.gloss: to put; to set; to become (ponerse + adj)

meanings.en: to put; to set; to become (ponerse + adj)
meanings.note: Irregular: pongo, pon, puse, puesto; ponerse nervioso = get nervous.

examples.text: Pongo dos tazas limpias en la mesa.
examples.trans: I put two clean cups on the table.

examples.text: Pon la maleta junto al mostrador.
examples.trans: Set the suitcase beside the counter.

meanings.note: Shortens to primer before masculine singular nouns (el primer día); also used as adverb ('first').

examples.text: Hoy es mi primer día de trabajo.
examples.trans: Today is my first day of work.

examples.text: La primera habitación está libre.
examples.trans: The first room is vacant.

meanings.note: Core connector and relative pronoun (unaccented, distinct from interrogative qué).

examples.text: Espero que descanses muy bien.
examples.trans: I hope that you rest very well.

examples.text: El pan de esta panadería huele genial.
examples.trans: The bread that The baker bakes smells great.

meanings.note: Hacer ruido = make noise; hay ruido = it is noisy.

examples.text: El ruido está aquí.
examples.trans: The noise is here.

examples.text: Vemos los ruidos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the noises from the door.

meanings.note: Sala de conciertos = concert hall; sala de la caldera = boiler room.

examples.text: La sala está aquí.
examples.trans: The hall is here.

examples.text: Vemos las salas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the halls from the door.

se.gloss: himself / herself / yourself / themselves; impersonal one

meanings.en: himself / herself / yourself / themselves; impersonal one
meanings.note: Reflexive, reciprocal, passive/impersonal pronoun, and indirect object le/les before lo/la.

examples.text: La puerta se abre despacio.
examples.trans: The door opens slowly.

examples.text: Aquí se oye el canto de los pájaros.
examples.trans: Here you can hear the birds singing.

meanings.note: As a masculine noun (el secreto), means 'secret'.

examples.text: Es una pieza secreta.
examples.trans: It is a secret piece.

examples.text: Claro, Mateo, ¡tu secreto está a salvo con nosotras!
examples.trans: Sure, Mateo, your secret is safe with us!

meanings.note: Seguro que... = I bet / probably...

examples.text: Es una pieza segura.
examples.trans: It is a sure piece.

examples.text: ¿Está segura? ¡Parece preciosa y muy calentita!
examples.trans: Are you sure? It looks lovely and nice and warm!

meanings.note: Las seis = six o'clock.

examples.text: Me despierto a las seis y media.
examples.trans: I wake up at six thirty.

examples.text: Tengo seis limones en la cesta.
examples.trans: I have six lemons in the basket.

meanings.note: Fin de semana = weekend; la semana que viene = next week.

examples.text: La semana está aquí.
examples.trans: The week is here.

examples.text: Vemos las semanas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the weeks from the door.

ser.gloss: to be (identity, origin, time, permanent trait)

meanings.en: to be (identity, origin, time, permanent trait)
meanings.note: Used for names, professions, ownership (es mía), materials (es de madera), and clock time.

examples.text: Soy arquitecta y vivo en Valencia.
examples.trans: I am an architect and live in Valencia.

examples.text: Esa maleta azul es mía.
examples.trans: That blue suitcase is mine.

meanings.note: Unaccented conjunction, distinct from accented sí ('yes').

examples.text: Avísame si necesitas otra manta.
examples.trans: Let me know if you need another blanket.

examples.text: Mira si queda leche en la nevera.
examples.trans: Check whether any milk is left in the fridge.

meanings.note: Same form for masculine and feminine.

examples.text: Es una pieza suave.
examples.trans: It is a soft piece.

examples.text: Y mire: esta chaqueta de lana suave está limpia y nueva. Pruébela.
examples.trans: And look: this soft wool cardigan is clean and unworn. Try it on.

subir.gloss: to go up; to climb; to carry upstairs

meanings.en: to go up; to climb; to carry upstairs
meanings.note: Works both intransitively and transitively.

examples.text: Subo las toallas limpias a la primera planta.
examples.trans: I carry the clean towels up to the first floor.

examples.text: Subieron despacio la escalera de madera.
examples.trans: They climbed the wooden stairs slowly.

meanings.note: Brick basement beneath a building.

examples.text: El sótano está aquí.
examples.trans: The cellar is here.

examples.text: Vemos los sótanos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the cellars from the door.

meanings.note: Indoor ceiling (distinct from outdoor tiled tejado).

examples.text: El techo está aquí.
examples.trans: The ceiling is here.

examples.text: Vemos los techos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the ceilings from the door.

tener.gloss: to have; to have to (tener que + inf)

meanings.en: to have; to have to (tener que + inf)
meanings.note: Used in idioms: tener hambre/frío/miedo/prisa/razón; tener que = must.

examples.text: Tenemos ocho habitaciones tranquilas.
examples.trans: We have eight quiet rooms.

examples.text: Tengo que cerrar la ventana ahora.
examples.trans: I have to close the window now.

terminar.gloss: to finish (terminar de + inf = finish doing)

meanings.en: to finish (terminar de + inf = finish doing)
meanings.note: Regular -ar verb.

examples.text: Termino mi turno a las tres.
examples.trans: I finish my shift at three.

examples.text: Terminamos de pintar antes de comer.
examples.trans: We finished painting before lunch.

meanings.note: A classic Spanish breakfast is una tostada con tomate.

examples.text: Para desayunar quiero una tostada con tomate.
examples.trans: For breakfast I want toast with tomato.

examples.text: Las tostadas están en la mesa.
examples.trans: The toast is on the table.

meanings.note: Used for people working (machines use funcionar).

examples.text: Trabajo en recepción de lunes a viernes.
examples.trans: I work at the front desk Monday through Friday.

examples.text: Hoy trabajamos todos en equipo.
examples.trans: Today we all worked as a team.

meanings.note: Forms: un (m sg), una (f sg), unos (m pl 'some/about'), unas (f pl).

examples.text: Quiero un café caliente, por favor.
examples.trans: I would like a hot coffee, please.

examples.text: Hay una mesa libre en el patio.
examples.trans: There is a free table in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Una ventana soleada = a sunny window.

examples.text: La ventana está aquí.
examples.trans: The window is here.

examples.text: Vemos las ventanas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the windows from the door.

meanings.note: Irregular: veo, vi, visto.

examples.text: Desde aquí veo el puente de piedra.
examples.trans: From here I see the stone bridge.

examples.text: ¡Nos vemos luego en el patio!
examples.trans: See you later in the courtyard!

meanings.note: Changes to e before words starting with /i/ sound (i- or hi-).

examples.text: Servimos café caliente y pan fresco.
examples.trans: We serve hot coffee and fresh bread.

examples.text: Son las siete y cuarto.
examples.trans: It is quarter past seven.
